unit.subject: English
unit.unitOverview: This is your capstone: a celebration of your first year of English. You will choose your favourite work for a picture-and-word portfolio, make a six-page mini-book, give a one-minute presentation, and think about what you would like to learn next. Everything you have learned this year comes together here.
unit.learningPath:
Choose favourite work.
Review 30 useful words.
Listen to the capstone story and project brief.
Make a six-page picture-and-word book.
Practise and share a one-minute presentation.
Complete the checkpoint and supported reflection.
howToUse: This is your capstone: one big project that uses everything you learned this year. There is no video — start by reading about the project.
In Reading there are three texts: the story “Amal's English Year”, the project brief “My Capstone Steps”, and the “Celebration Dialogue”. Listen to them and read along.
In Writing you make your own six-page picture-and-word book. Draw, write, and make it better.
In Speaking you practise a one-minute talk about your book. Say it to your family, or record it.
The Final course quiz is on this page, after every section has a tick. It is extra — it does not lock the unit.

readings.title: Amal's English Year
readings.theme: celebrating Grade 1 words, stories, speaking and early writing
readings.passageScript:
It was the last week of Grade 1, and Amal wanted to remember everything she had learned. She opened her big learning folder and looked inside. There were letters from the very first week, family pictures she had drawn, colourful games, shapes and numbers, farm animals, and pictures about her five senses. She also found vehicles, water experiments, and pictures of town places like the shop and the library.

“I did so much this year!” said Amal. She chose her favourite pieces of work and made a new book. She called it My First English World.

On celebration day, Amal stood at the front of the class with her new book. She pointed to the pages and read a few words out loud. “My name is Amal,” she said. “I can speak English. I like my book.”

Everyone clapped for Amal. She felt very proud of everything she had learned that year.

readings.title: My Capstone Steps
readings.theme: celebrating Grade 1 words, stories, speaking and early writing
readings.passageScript: Now it is time to make your very own capstone book! First, choose three favourite pieces of work from this year. Next, make a six-page picture-and-word book, adding a label and a short pattern sentence to each page. Then practise saying a one-minute show-and-tell about your book — say what you made and what you learned. Share it with your teacher if you have one, or with a family member, or practise it by yourself in front of a mirror. Finally, complete your reflection page.
readings.reviewStatus: Needs re-review (content updated for self-sufficiency pass)

readings.title: Celebration Dialogue
readings.theme: celebrating Grade 1 words, stories, speaking and early writing
readings.passageScript:
It was celebration day, and Amal was ready to share her book. Her teacher smiled and asked her some questions.

Teacher: What is your favourite page?
Learner: I like my family page best.
Teacher: What can you say about it?
Learner: This is my mum. I love my family.
Teacher: Well done! What is your next goal for English?
Learner: I will read more words next year.

grammar.title: Introduce yourself with confidence
grammar.explanation: You have learned so much this year. Say your name clearly and proudly to someone new.
grammar.commonMistake: A quiet mumble is easy to miss. Take a breath first, then say the name slowly and loudly.
grammar.memoryTip: Look up, smile, then speak. That is a strong start every time.
grammar.practice: Introduce yourself to three people: My name is Maya. My name is Sami. My name is Theo.

grammar.title: Show off everything you can do now
grammar.explanation: Look back at your whole year. Name the new things you can do in English.
grammar.commonMistake: Children may repeat the same skill each time. Try a different 'I can' in every sentence.
grammar.memoryTip: Count on your fingers and try to reach five different 'I can' sentences.
grammar.practice: Say three new skills: I can read words. I can count to twenty. I can spell my name.

grammar.title: Tell someone your favourites
grammar.explanation: Share what you love most. Say 'I like' and add your favourite thing or activity.
grammar.commonMistake: Some children say 'I am like books.' The word 'am' is not needed here: 'I like books.'
grammar.memoryTip: Put both hands on your heart when you say 'I like'.
grammar.practice: Say three favourites: I like stories. I like drawing. I like parties.

grammar.title: Name any object with confidence
grammar.explanation: Name anything near you. Say 'a' before most words, but 'an' before a vowel sound: a cup, an umbrella.
grammar.commonMistake: Children pop 'a' before umbrella by mistake. Before an a, e, i, o, u sound we say 'an': an umbrella, an apple.
grammar.memoryTip: If the word starts with an open-mouth sound — a, e, i, o, u — use 'an'.
grammar.practice: Name three things: This is a cup. This is an apple. This is a chair.

grammar.title: Add a describing word to any thing
grammar.explanation: After you name a thing, describe it. Choose a colour, a size or a feeling word.
grammar.commonMistake: Children sometimes name the object twice instead of describing it. Ask yourself 'What is it like?' to find a describing word.
grammar.memoryTip: Name it first, describe it second. Two sentences make a strong pair.
grammar.practice: Name and describe three: It is blue. It is small. It is lovely.

grammar.title: Set your next English goal
grammar.explanation: Think about what you would love to learn next, then say it out loud to your teacher.
grammar.commonMistake: Some children describe what they can already do. A goal is something new, not learned yet.
grammar.memoryTip: Point forward as you speak, because a goal is out ahead of you.

activities.title: Portfolio treasure hunt
activities.instructionsAndItems: Hunt through your folder for: 1. your neatest writing, 2. a picture you coloured, 3. a word list, 4. work you found hard. Show your favourite to an adult if one is nearby, or look back over it yourself and say why you chose it.
activities.answerSummary: Four pieces found in the folder: their neatest writing, a coloured picture, a word list, and work they found hard. Accept their own judgement on neatest and hardest, then listen to their favourite.
activities.deliveryMode: Shared UI and live teacher session
activities.reviewStatus: Needs re-review (content updated for self-sufficiency pass)

activities.title: Thirty-word picture sort
activities.instructionsAndItems: Spread out thirty word cards from this year. Sort them into piles: school, family, animals and town. Read each pile aloud to an adult if one is nearby, or read each pile aloud to yourself.
activities.answerSummary: Thirty cards sorted into school, family, animals and town piles, then each pile read aloud. Accept any card placed where the child can justify it, and words read with your finger underneath.
activities.deliveryMode: Shared UI and live teacher session
activities.reviewStatus: Needs re-review (content updated for self-sufficiency pass)

activities.title: Story retell with pictures
activities.instructionsAndItems: Put four story pictures in order. Retell the story using 'First', 'Then', 'Next' and 'Last'. Ask an adult to listen twice if one is nearby, or say it aloud to yourself twice.
activities.answerSummary: Four story pictures in the correct order, retold using First, Then, Next and Last. Accept an order self-corrected on the second telling, and the four linking words used in any sensible sequence.
activities.deliveryMode: Shared UI and live teacher session
activities.reviewStatus: Needs re-review (content updated for self-sufficiency pass)

activities.title: Mini-book making
activities.instructionsAndItems: Make your mini-book. 1. Fold three sheets. 2. Staple the middle. 3. Add your six pages. 4. Draw a cover with your name on it.
activities.answerSummary: Three sheets folded, stapled through the middle by an adult, six pages added inside, and a cover carrying their name. Accept uneven folds and a name in wobbly or reversed letters.
activities.deliveryMode: Shared UI and live teacher session

activities.title: One-minute rehearsal
activities.instructionsAndItems: Rehearse your talk for one minute. An adult can time you if one is nearby, or you can count slowly to sixty yourself, or use a clock. Stand tall, speak slowly, and hold your book so everyone can see it.
activities.answerSummary: A full minute of talking while you time them, standing tall, speaking slowly and holding the book turned outwards. Accept around forty seconds of real speaking and one pause to find their place.
activities.deliveryMode: Shared UI and live teacher session
activities.reviewStatus: Needs re-review (content updated for self-sufficiency pass)

activities.title: Celebration showcase
activities.instructionsAndItems: Show your book at the class celebration. 1. Greet everyone. 2. Read two pages. 3. Say your next goal. 4. Thank your family.
activities.answerSummary: A greeting, two pages read, one next goal said and a thank you to family. Accept pages recited from memory, a very simple goal such as 'read more', and quiet thanks with a nod.
activities.deliveryMode: Shared UI and live teacher session

assignments.title: My First English World capstone
assignments.instructions: Celebrate your first year of English. 1) Choose three favourite pieces of work and put them in a folder. 2) Make a six-page mini-book with one picture and one word on every page, choosing from letters, family, farm, senses, travel, water and town words. 3) Record a one-minute talk: My name is ___. I can ___. I like ___. This is a ___. It is ___. 4) End by telling us: My next goal is ___.

quizzes.question: Which word completes the sentence: My name ___ Maya.
quizzes.explanation: My name is one thing, so we use is; are is for more than one and am only goes with I.

quizzes.question: Which word completes the sentence: I ___ hop on one foot.
quizzes.explanation: Can tells what you are able to do; is and are do not go with I hop, and the is not a doing word.

quizzes.question: Which one is a complete sentence?
quizzes.options: cat this | a cat | This is a cat. | is cat
quizzes.explanation: It starts with a capital letter, makes sense and ends with a full stop; the others are just groups of words.

quizzes.question: Which word names a colour?
quizzes.explanation: Blue is a colour; a bus is a vehicle, a farm is a place and hear is a sense word.

quizzes.question: Which word names a person in a family?
quizzes.explanation: Mum is a family member; the other words start with m too but they are a place, the sky and a thing.

quizzes.question: Which word is an action you do in a ball game?
quizzes.explanation: Bounce is an action with a ball; a hospital is a place, water is a liquid and a triangle is a shape.

quizzes.question: Which one is an animal that lives on a farm?
quizzes.explanation: A goat is a farm animal; a bus, a pencil and a river are not animals.

quizzes.question: Which body part helps you hear the school bell?
quizzes.explanation: We hear with our ears; eyes see, hands touch and the nose smells.

quizzes.question: Which sentence tells a safe thing to do in the town?
quizzes.options: Stop at the red light. | Run into the road. | Drop litter on the path. | Push people at the bus stop.
quizzes.explanation: Stopping at a red light keeps you safe; the other actions are dangerous or unkind.

quizzes.question: What should you do before you show your capstone project to the class?
quizzes.options: Rub out all the words. | Practise it and check it. | Hide every page. | Skip the reflection.
quizzes.explanation: Practising and checking helps you share your best work; the other choices would spoil it.

Accept any correct sentence built on the pattern “My name is ___.” Model answers: My name is Maya. My name is Sami. My name is Theo. Watch for: A quiet mumble is easy to miss. Take a breath first, then say the name slowly and loudly.

Accept any correct sentence built on the pattern “I can ___.” Model answers: I can read words. I can count to twenty. I can spell my name. Watch for: Children may repeat the same skill each time. Encourage a different 'I can' in every sentence.

Accept any correct sentence built on the pattern “I like ___.” Model answers: I like stories. I like drawing. I like parties. Watch for: Some children say 'I am like books.' The word 'am' is not needed here: 'I like books.'

Accept any correct sentence built on the pattern “This is a / an ___.” Model answers: This is a cup. This is an apple. This is a chair. Watch for: Children pop 'a' before umbrella by mistake. Before an a, e, i, o, u sound we say 'an': an umbrella, an apple.

Accept any correct sentence built on the pattern “It is ___.” Model answers: It is blue. It is small. It is lovely. Watch for: Children sometimes name the object twice instead of describing it. Ask 'What is it like?' to get a describing word.

Accept any correct sentence built on the pattern “My next goal is ___.” Model answers: My next goal is to read a book. My next goal is to write a story. My next goal is to spell ten words. Watch for: Some children describe what they can already do. A goal is something new, not learned yet.
